releaseNotes.title: Release notes
releaseNotes.subtitle: What’s new from v0.1.0 to v0.2.0. Notes are grouped by topic so you can scan what matters to you.

v020.intro: This release focuses on safer, clearer OAuth redirects, better visibility when something must be migrated, and new sign-in options on the Accounts API side—including Microsoft, Apple, and GitHub OAuth. Use the sections below to see each area at a glance.

oauthApi.title: Microsoft, Apple & GitHub OAuth (Accounts API)
oauthApi.lead: Besides Google, the Accounts API can complete the same login flow for Microsoft (Entra ID / Azure AD), Sign in with Apple, and GitHub OAuth Apps. You register each provider like before; callback and “get link” behaviour stay familiar.
oauthApi.i1: Microsoft: uses the Microsoft identity platform (multi-tenant `common`), exchanges the auth code for tokens, and reads the profile from Microsoft Graph.
oauthApi.i2: Apple: uses Sign in with Apple’s authorize URL; the token step uses Apple’s required JWT client secret (configured with your Team ID, Key ID, and `.p8` private key—see Accounts API docs).
oauthApi.i3: In the admin, you still choose the provider when building or testing OAuth links; no separate screen only for Microsoft or Apple.
oauthApi.i4: Shared internals: user profile is normalized the same way as Google so tokens and user records stay consistent across providers.
oauthApi.i5: GitHub: OAuth App flow (`github.com/login/oauth`), token exchange, and profile via the GitHub REST API with `read:user` and `user:email` scopes (see Accounts API docs for registering the OAuth App and callback URL).

redirects.title: Redirects & migration
redirects.i1: Whitelist several redirect URLs per platform (web, mobile, desktop) instead of relying on a single legacy field.
redirects.i2: Optional opaque token (`rt`) in the OAuth state when you need to target one whitelist row from the “get link” dialog.
redirects.i3: If old redirect columns are still in use, the app prompts you to move values into the whitelist—notifications and OAuth Providers link you to the fix.

adminUi.title: Notifications & OAuth in the admin
adminUi.i1: Notifications page lists pending work (for example OAuth redirect migration) so it doesn’t get lost.
adminUi.i2: OAuth link dialog: pick platform, role, optional destination redirect, then copy the provider’s authorization URL.
adminUi.i3: Sidebar shows a subtle alert on the account menu when OAuth migration still needs attention.

usersBranding.title: Users & branding
usersBranding.i1: User detail: change the user’s role from the profile and small actions like copying an email from a login method.
usersBranding.i2: Favicon updated to match the Accounts branding.

meta.title: Language & version
meta.i1: New and updated English/Spanish strings for OAuth redirects, migration, and notifications.

v010.intro: The first public admin slice for Accounts: manage apps, users, and integrations, with Google OAuth and session login.

foundation.title: Core areas
foundation.i1: Dashboard, users, roles & policies, webhooks, API keys, OAuth providers, behaviors, email templates, tokens, and settings.
foundation.i2: Central place to work with your Accounts app and related configuration.

security.title: API access & login
security.i1: Secret API Key to call Accounts from the admin (stored client-side when you save it).
security.i2: Session-backed login and BFF routes so the browser talks to Accounts safely.

oauthGoogle.title: Google OAuth
oauthGoogle.i1: Configure Google as an OAuth provider and run the standard authorization + callback flow with Accounts.
oauthGoogle.i2: Same patterns you still use today; v0.2.0 extends them to more providers and redirect rules.

experience.title: Look & language
experience.i2: English and Spanish UI, plus a link to documentation from the account menu.

hints.detailsRedirects: Current list of valid redirects used to issue OAuth links. Each row has a unique «rt» token and appears here as soon as the backend registers it. If empty, links can only be issued from legacy columns (deprecated in v1.0.0).
hints.provider: Pick the external provider (Google, Microsoft, Apple, or GitHub). Once created it cannot be changed — you'd need to delete the config and create a new one.
hints.clientId: Public identifier issued by the provider when you registered your OAuth app. Find it in the provider's console (Google Cloud Console, Microsoft Entra, etc.).
hints.clientSecret: Secret credential issued by the provider. Used only server-side to exchange the code for a token. When editing, leave empty to keep the current one.
hints.callback: The backend generates a unique endpoint (Callback URI) that you must register in the provider's console as an «Authorized redirect URI». The Callback Key is the opaque part of that URL. Click «Generate» to mint a new pair.
hints.scopes: OAuth permissions your app requests from the provider (space-separated). The default «email profile openid» covers basic login. Check the provider's docs for additional scopes (Drive, Calendar, etc.).
hints.redirectWhitelist: Allowed redirect URLs after authentication. Each row gets a stable «rt» token that travels in OAuth links. Removing a row invalidates any previously shared link using that URL. You must include at least one with platform Web.
hints.platform: Determines what kind of URL is valid: «web» for https URLs, «android/ios» for deep links (custom scheme like app://), «desktop» typically localhost. Affects the OAuth flow (PKCE, token handling, etc.).
hints.rowName: Internal label to identify this row (e.g. «Production», «Staging», «Local»). Does not affect the OAuth flow — only helps you remember which environment this URL belongs to.
hints.linkRtField: Opaque identifier for the redirect row. Auto-filled from the URL chosen above; only manually editable when there are no whitelist redirects (legacy mode).
hints.migrationBanner: Some providers have redirects stored only in legacy columns (redirect_uri_*). Click «Run migration» to copy them into the current whitelist. In v1.0.0 the legacy fields will stop being used to issue links.

strategy.helper: Default is Random. Switch to Fixed only when you need a predictable code for QA or automated testing.

tooltips.verificationActive: When active, the user must confirm a code sent to their email before signing in.
tooltips.codeSize: Number of characters in the code (typical: 6).
tooltips.ttlSec: Lifetime in seconds for the code. After that the user must request a new one.
tooltips.codeType: Alphabet of the code. 'numeric' = digits 0-9 only. 'alphanumeric' = digits + letters a-z and A-Z.
tooltips.codeStrategy: How the code is generated. 'Random' uses a cryptographic RNG (recommended and required in production). 'Fixed' always returns the same value — only allowed in testing environments: local, development, staging, qa, test.
tooltips.fixedCode: Value returned literally as the verification code. Must match the configured size and alphabet. Only allowed when ENVIRONMENT is local, development, staging, qa, or test. In production the backend rejects activation with HTTP 422.
tooltips.autoSignup: When on, a magic link to an unknown email creates the account. When off, only existing accounts can sign in.
tooltips.redirectBaseUrl: Origin of the email link (e.g. https://lyron.lat). The final path is concatenated server-side.
tooltips.defaultRedirectPath: Must start with '/'. No '//', no ':' (schemes), max 512 chars.
